3990486954: The average human brain can only remember seven things at once.  That's six better than the average sack brain of course.  But that's why sackpeople invented MEMORISERS, which save valuable information in a handy popit-sized container.  Go get one from the ADVANCED LOGIC bit of yer TOOLS BAG.  A MEMORISER can have up to a gazillion of inputs and outputs, but for now we just want three.  Connect up the tag sensors to each input.  We're going to transfer the position of each of these pistons over to the other set of pistons over here...  ...so connect those up too.  Now it's essential all the pistons are set to POSITIONAL. This permits a signal that isn't just on or off, but any value in between.  Half on, for example. Or half off, if you're a glass half airy type of person.  Now just attach that BUTTON to the TRIGGER INPUT of the MEMORISER  and then we're done.  Each time Sackboy hits the button, the positions of the pistons on the left are saved in the MEMORISER and relayed to the pistons on the right.  Even if the first pistons keep moving, the MEMORISER keeps the values when you last triggered it.  Want to hear something exciting?  If you add a LABEL  The memoriser can share values with other memorisers of the same label  But what's more, the memoriser will REMEMBER the values. Even when you leave the level, and come back!  Imagine the possibilities! Perhaps a diary assistant, who can help me remember my appointment with... um, thingy... at the wotsitplace... Oh dear, see what I mean?

4292468265: Oooh, stickers stickers stickers, the 3 S’s.  We all love stickers, but laying them thirty deep makes everything get gummed up.  Using one or two will keep the neighbourhood bright and tidy.  Some things might look impressive but they also make the thermometer level rise.  You might need to cull a few sticker panels,  smoke machines  holograms,  and keep those atmospheric effects to a minimum. It’s just an idea... Cruel to be kind and all that.  When it comes to lighting, surfaces on LittleBigPlanet will only reflect two lights at the same time.  More than that will be ignored, or might even start conflicting, and we don't want that.  This is “mood lighting”, not “walking off in a huff” lighting.  It's fab filling the Imagisphere with your own funky ditties using a MUSIC SEQUENCER, but sometimes you just want to hear an old classic with a MUSIC OBJECT.  What's more, it lets our friend in the thermometer kick back and relax a bit too. He especially likes the NON-INTERACTIVE tunes.  Here's another energy saving tip from the Department Of The Patently Obvious.  With less stuff visible on-screen,  the smoother and groovier your scene will run.  This applies to cameras too. Zoom them in for added drama and impactfulnicity. That's not a word. But that's OK. We're all friends here.  When it comes to levels, less is more – something of a mathematical anomaly, but it's true!  If you have lots of things going on in your scene, why not split it into two levels.  Less clutter, more levels. Everyone's a winner!  Like any city, it's a good idea to distribute your Sackbot population if you want to avoid overcrowding.  It eases congestion of the Imagisphere and you avoid saying “excuse me” every five seconds.  Sackbots are intelligent beings so don't just let them wander aimlessly. Give them something to do.  Use logic and behaviours to give them specific tasks.  If you RECORD a Sackbot animation then it will carry on to its heart's content and won't expend any valuable brain power on the task.  I hope you're not one of these people who leaves the telly on when you leave the room, because the Imagisphere doesn't appreciate that sort of behaviour.  If you have some complex logic beeping and booping when you don't need it, turn it off!  Wireless logic seems like a great gimmick, and indeed it is. TAG SENSOR and the like.  But if you need extra space in your gorgeously complicated scene then we recommend good old fashioned wires.  Oh go on, show them off! They work hard and deserve a bit of recognition.  We've learnt so much, you and I. But the Imagisphere always has more to teach. Open your mind and let your imagination run free...  ...make something wonderfully amazing!

It is THE most efficient mode of quad-dimensional propulsion.  Remember to TWEAK the SPEED and ACCELERATION – jogging speed or plodding. In the Tweak Menu, ALLOW PUSHING will let your foot shove obstacles out of the way, up to the specified MAXIMUM PUSH WEIGHT, which is measured in numbers of Sackpersons.  The INPUT ACTION gives all sorts of options of how your foot moves in and out. Dare I say it..? Have a faff!  So connect that switch to the IN/OUT MOVER. And I'll tell you a useful shortcut: You can disconnect the wire from the ADVANCED MOVER by pressing the ACTION BUTTON on it, then move it down and connect it to the IN/OUT MOVER'S INPUT. 1328615271: In the MENU LEVEL, place another MEMORISER.  Once again, three INPUT PORTS will do us proud.  And the LABEL –  let's give it the same “rolls-off-the-tongue” label as the last one.  Here's the mind-shakingly awesome bit:  MEMORISERS with the same LABEL will all contain the very same data – even when they're on completely different levels.  How? Science!  Connect the first OUTPUT of the MEMORISER to the STICKER PANEL with the BRONZE STAR on it.  And do likewise and similarly for SILVER and GOLD.  The SCORE STARS in the MENU LEVEL will be triggered if the player gets enough points to trigger the SCORE SENSORS in the ACTUAL LEVEL.  Ingenious isn't it!  The final task is setting up the LINK into the next scene.  It's activated by a TOUCH SENSOR, but that STICKER PANEL is blocking the sensor.  You see where we're going with this?  The LEVEL LINK is effectively locked until the STICKER PANEL is deactivated.  So connect the first OUTPUT of the MEMORISER to a NOT GATE  then from there to the STICKER PANEL.  And our menu is complete!  When the first level is completed, the MEMORISER will be triggered and unlock the next level link.  It's guaranteed to stop naughty Sack-personages skipping to the next level. And yes: I AM looking at you.

With the ACT behaviour, you can record your own movements directly into your SACKBOT’S grey matter.  You only have to do something embarrassing once, but your SACKBOT stooge will have to do it as often as you want him to.  PLAY ONCE makes him do it just the once,  but you can also LOOP him.  LOOP RELATIVE makes him do it wherever he's standing.  But LOOP ABSOLUTE will return him to his exact starting point each time his embarrassment ends.  SACKBOTS also have their own MICROCHIP.  Select SHOW CIRCUITBOARD or press the R button to reveal it.  Why not place BEHAVIOURS straight onto his MICROCHIP.  Good deeds, ill will, indifferent acts of blasé thoughtlessness – whatever you think of.  Trigger them with SENSORS, but remember it’s the most recently activated BEHAVIOUR that controls him.  So if you set him to HOSTILE he may very well come after you!  I don't know about hostile, seems rather over-friendly to me...  Better not put a Danger Tweaker on that Microchip.  I’d show him some respect if I were you.  Give him a voice. Yes!  Put a MAGIC MOUTH on his MICROCHIP  then set the ACTOR NAME of the MAGIC MOUTH to something urbane and witty. The SPEECH options allow you to choose what manner of noises will emanate from your magic mouth.  You can even RECORD your own voices and put those into the scene. Go on, have a tinker and see if you can't find the perfect ZOOM and ANGLE to show off our guest's mouldiest side.  Hey, you should make Cheddar George your co-host. 3424036509: To be a master materialist, there are a few new tricks you need to learn.  Open your Popit by TAPPING the POPIT BUTTON, and bring forth your GOODIES BAG.  We're going to choose a STAR SHAPE.  Now it's tool time. TOUCH and HOLD this button, then SLIDE up to the top.  See? It says STAMP. Let go of your finger on top of it, and let's find out what it does.  The STAMP tool will place exactly one block of the shape you choose. None of that artful smearing, just pixel-perfect precision. TAP it down decisively.  STAMPING it into another material will create a perfect CUT OUT and both shapes will be GLUED together.  Open your slidey set of tools again and this time choose the ERASER.  The ERASER deletes all craft material as you drag it across the screen. A sort of ANTI-PAINT BRUSH.  Go back again for the HOLE PUNCH.  This also deletes material, but only one hole exactly where you tap.  When you feel ready, press the BACK button a few times to get out of popit.  Get the POPIT CURSOR, then TAP the tree to select it.  Now let's TWEAK the tree.  Press the MENU BUTTON or TAP the TWEAK BUTTON and the TWEAK MENU appears.  TWEAK MENUS let you tinker with the properties of almost anything on LittleBigPlanet  Tap here for the first tweak setting.  This setting is called PHYSICS PROPERTIES. If you set this to STATIC the tree will not move, no matter what happens to it.  Mmm.. Yes.  Set it to DYNAMIC and it can be moved and manipulated by other things.  Think of your scene like a machine. There’s no sense putting a motor in something that’s never going to move is there! All of your energy should be saved for the most important parts.  So, if you make all of the things that don’t really need to move into STATIC OBJECTS, your beautiful somewheres will run as smooth as clockwork  Clever stuff, eh? So get crafting!

3966264967: Sackboy's pioneering the new musical genre of Shampoo Moko. Apparently it mainly involves singing in the shower.  Okay, let’s lay down some tracks. You can get a MUSIC SEQUENCER from the MUSIC PAGE.  The R BUTTON will open or close its CIRCUIT BOARD.  It’s here you place INSTRUMENTS to build your fab and groovy gramophone tunes.  You really have to TWEAK fiddle and faff with the INSTRUMENTS to get your own sounds. Seriously. This is how I created Off Key White Noise Yelling. All the kids are into it now.  Press the MENU button to open an instrument.  Each INSTRUMENT plays according to a PATTERN. Move the cursor around the pattern with the LEFT STICK and place down new notes with the ACTION BUTTON.  The R and L BUTTONS lengthen or shorten your notes.  UP and DOWN on the RIGHT STICK will change the VOLUME of the note.  LEFT and RIGHT will change its TIMBRE – the quality and uniqueness of the instrument.  It’s not as complex as it sounds and if you mess up UNDO and REDO with the LEFT and RIGHT BUTTONS.  The UP BUTTON will pause and play, letting you preview your musical mayhem.  Once completed you can TWEAK the INSTRUMENT by pressing the MENU BUTTON as there may be further adjustments to KEY and SCALE you’d like to include.  If your composition's becoming a magnum opus, which is Latin for a “big deal”, you can use the REAR TOUCH PAD to pan along your sequence like so.  When you’re done, rearrange your INSTRUMENTS on the MUSIC SEQUENCER’s circuit board in any order you choose.  So, can we hear what you’ve been composing?  Take it away!  No seriously, take it away. There’s a BUTTON in the GAMEPLAY KITS page. That’s it.  Place it on the ground near Mildly Amusing Bunny.  Now with the cursor, grab the BUTTON’s OUTPUT TAB. You drag these TABS to wire up all electrical gadgets on LittleBigPlanet.  Connect it to the MOTOR BOLT.  Now it’s wired up, Bunny’s face will only spin when the BUTTON is pressed.  See, now that’s funny! Funnier, at least. Funny-ish.  Let's go back to your TOOLS BAG.  Right. What else? GRAB SENSORS! They’re useful.  You activate these by GRABBING the thing they're stuck onto.  So let's connect our GRAB SENSOR to that MOTOR BOLT.  Wouldn't you know it, it works!  2-WAY and 3-WAY SWITCHES are available as well. The 2-WAY is yer basic on/off switch.  The 3-WAY however can be pulled either forwards or backwards, and you can decide how far you want to pull it... Here's how.  When you attach a SWITCH, you can change how it controls the MOTOR BOLT.  Tweak the MOTOR BOLT and look at the INPUT ACTION.  On/off just turns on the motor in the direction you set.  With FORWARDS BACKWARDS the motor turns a different direction depending on which way you pull the switch.  SINGLE CYCLE turns it all the way round once then stops, even if you let go half way!  Finally SPEED SCALE makes the motor turn faster the further you pull the switch!  It's a treasure trove of gem-like possibilities. Try them all!  By the way, did you know you can pause these videos whenever you like via the START MENU?  Not that you ever would. I mean what could be more important than--  --listening to me. I ask you. 1108139899: Moving pictures aren't the same without moving cameras. In LittleBigPlanet you can string several cameras together to make one epic shot!  Okay, dig out the MOVIE CAMERA from the CAMERAS SECTION of the TOOLS BAG.  First of all, you'll want to place a few of them.  Then use the POPIT CURSOR to connect the OUTPUT of one CAMERA to the INPUT of the next.  Now, TWEAKS are the order of the day here.  TWEAK the ANGLE and ZOOM to set up your shots.  TWEAKING the HOLD TIME of a MOVIE CAMERA sets how long it will wait in that camera position.  The TRANSITION TIME is how long it takes to move from the previous camera position into this one.  What's a TRANSITION I hear you ask? Well, this is how it changes from one camera to the next. Some experimental faffing really pays dividends here, so let's leave it as a SOFT PAN for now.  By pressing the R BUTTON you can flit to the next CAMERA, and the L BUTTON to jump back. It’s easier than it sounds.  Okay, time to roll cameras, Sackboy. What is this by the way? 1199171102: Only your closest friends will tell you that you have your bowler hat inside out.  Similarly, up here, only a true friend will tell you when your scene is overcrowded, and the tall fellow in the tube on the left is that friend.  He's a measuring stick for productivity. He gets taller the more you build.  But when he's getting too big for his tube, it's a sign you're running out of space too.  You're going to need a few tricks to OPTIMISE your scene.  Fortunately for you, we have lots.  Sometimes you can save space in your scene by not having over-complicated shapes in it.  This means fewer VERTICES. Y'know, the dots you see when using the corner editor.  Dashed useful they are but somewhat elaborate if you’re short on space.  Perfect circles are the exception that proves the rule because they have no corners.  But if you edit them... whoops! – you'll have dots before your eyes once more  Thinking big has got me into trouble a few times, so I taught myself to think smaller but more often!  If you've built a mega-ginormous-ultra-shape, cut it up into several smaller ones.  Now that's much more manageable.  Even better, get rid of those bits which are off-screen and players will never see.  You can Tweak objects to make them STATIC.  Static objects keep themselves to themselves and don't interact with things around them.  Some OBJECTS don’t depend on connections with other things. The OBJECTS that you’ve discovered during your travels head straight in to the COLLECTED OBJECTS page. PINCH IN and OUT to re-size it.  ...and if you ROTATE your fingers around, the object will follow.  Just like every object in LittleBigPlanet you can mirror it by using the FLIP BUTTON.  You can move the object inwards and outwards by using the LAYERS MENU.  Hold down the L BUTTON to access it, then simply DRAG the middle of the LAYER SLIDER to move to your layer of choice. So he’s putting some lights and other malarkey up in preparation for this evening.  First thing is to find a TOGGLE in the ADVANCED LOGIC page in your TOOLS BAG.  TOGGLES send a constant signal that is either on or off. Each time a new signal is received the TOGGLE will switch on to off, or off to on.  Connect a button to the TOGGLE’s input  and a light to its OUTPUT.  Fabbo. Now when you step on Dark ’N’ Dangerous Bridge tonight you’ll be all lit up and safe.  Now, remember, you don’t want to be putting TOO many lights in your scene, or things might start going all flickery and weird...and besides, LittleBigPlanet is a verdant dreamscape, not a crass nightclub!  For further nocturnal safety you could make use of the super useful SELECTOR. Also to be found in the ADVANCED LOGIC shed.  Connect these 3 BUTTONS to the SELECTORS INPUTS  and the OUTPUTS to your bridge lights.  A SELECTOR will will only ever have one – that’s one, count it - one OUTPUT on at a time. This way you can turn the lights on as you cross the bridge without illuminating the lot and save the Imagisphere some energy to boot! Clean and green! 2545504479: Tag Radar may sound like the name of an alien private detective, but it is in fact a facility to track movement on either the PlayStation®3 system or PlayStation®Vita system and use that information to make something move on the other screen.   Yes yes, that sounds as clear as mud, I know, but this tricky maze will allow me to demonstrate.   So, take a gander at the PlayStation®Vita system screen.   You will see the maze that is also on the PlayStation®3 system screen. But what’s the difference?   Exactly!   On the PlayStation®Vita system there’s a tag on the box and a new chip which is the Tag Radar! Well spotted.   Give it a little tweak why don’t you?   Bring up your Popit cursor, highlight the Tag Radar chip and press the TWEAK button. You must ensure the tag type matches the colour of the tag on the box.   Well done.   Now, let’s move to the PlayStation®3 system and make the magic happen there too. Open up your Popit menu and select the Tag Radar from your Tools Bag. Place it on the maze in a similar spot to where it is on the PlayStation®Vita system screen.   Bring out your Popit cursor and tweak the Tag Radar and set it to ‘Receive’. Observe the ghost of the Tag that’s from the PlayStation®Vita system.  It’s not really a ghost, I just said that word to inject some mild peril.  Touch the box on the PlayStation®Vita system.  You see!  When you move it on the PlayStation®Vita system the Ghost Tag moves on the PlayStation®3 system. You liking that?  Try placing the box on the button. It’s great isn’t it. I can literally hear your brain whizzing with possibilities.  You go for it, squire.

• Exclusive Costumes – dress up your sack-buddy as a Space Pirate Captain, Space Pilot, Space Prison Warden, Holo Sackboy or in a Space Walk Suit.
• New Items – customise your world with a batch of stickers, objects, materials and decorations.
• New Tools and Gadgets – make your own Cross-Controller games, or play levels made by other LBP fans.

668000036: Now this piece of LittleBigPlanet technology is so clever, you could put it in a box and call it The Memoriser.  Oh. We kind of DID do that didn't we. Well, that proves my point. I think.  You can use The Memoriser to keep track of everything you do. Kind of like a diary, or an annoying little brother.  Let me show you how it works.  We're going to tell The Memoriser to remember the state of these lights at a precise moment in time.  First of all, you'll want to connect that bottom Toggle Switch to the 3rd input of the Memoriser.  Then, connect the 3rd output of the Memoriser to the bottom light panel on the right.  Now, as you can see, these 3 grab switches can be used to toggle the lights on the left off and on.  Perfect for creating the world's least flamboyant light show.  Now, if you connect the Remember button to the Memoriser's Trigger Input...  ...and then press the Remember button...  The Memoriser will remember that state, and put the lights on the right into exactly the same state.  Wonderful! And that is merely the first stop on our journey towards Amazingville.  Okay, now try grabbing the switches again to put the lights in a different state.  See how the lights on the right have stayed as they were?  That's because the Memoriser is still outputting the values you told it to remember.  A Memoriser is nothing if not obedient.  To make it forget these values, you need to reset the Memoriser.  Simply connect the Forget button to the Memoriser's Reset Input.  Jump on the button, and all of the remembered values will be forgotten.  Of course, the best way to learn something like this, is to have a good old-fashioned faff.  So feel free to play around with it as much as you like.

2979908434: Aha, you have one of those deliciously tactile PlayStation®Vita systems I see.  It’s like holding a little piece of hardware-heaven isn’t it. Delectation for y’digits.  And connected to your PlayStation®3 system too!? You’re a whiz, and you can cover me in wool and call me Sackboy if it aint so!  As before your best chum is y’Popit, so let’s meet it shall we. Open the Popit menu by pressing the POPIT BUTTON … and select the Goodies Bag.  We’re going to draw some material into the level … … and have a faff around with it so use your LEFT STICK and ACTION BUTTON to do so.  Or, use the fabulous TOUCHSCREEN facility, it’s your lifestyle choice.  You select objects by placing the Popit Cursor over them and pressing the … … ACTION BUTTON, … or by touching it using the TOUCHSCREEN.  Once selected, press and hold the L BUTTON.  Your keen eye will have no doubt spotted the panel that comes up on the right side of the TOUCHSCREEN.  This enables you to alter which layer it’s in by moving the LEFT STICK up and down and … you can change it from thin to thick by moving the RIGHT STICK up and down.  If wiggling sticks isn’t your thing then… you can also use your finger to move it from back to front and thick to thin.  Ah the wonder of your TOUCHSCREEN.It’s literally incandescent with interactivity. Try it. Slide your favourite finger across the screen and see how the Popit cursor instantly falls in love with you … and follows your every move.  This magic also works on objects within the game. They too form an instant attraction to you and obey your every deft finger swish. You can select things from your Popit menu via the gift of touch too. Amazing, but that’s just the start of it.  A PlayStation®Vita system has ultra modern sensors front and back, … making it practically sentient.  Use the REAR TOUCH PAD to, for example, move the camera around. One finger can pan the camera whilst another two of your digits control the zoom in and out. Of course, our old friend the Right Stick is there too to do the same job if you want.  Mustn’t forget old Righty.  You could dive in and start creating and sharing now if you like, … but hold your sack-horses a second.  What about the other buttons, bells and whistles? Are they there just to look gizmo-ish? No no and thrice no.  The button on the right of the PlayStation®Vita system screen is your POPIT BUTTON, … we’ve met this chappy before, … but press it again as it really is a joy to see how the Popit menu resplendently unfolds when touched.  Observe how the BACK BUTTON appears over the Popit Menus. Stylish. I could press that all day long. Touch the back button to close the Popit menu.  As you know, … the tweak facility is meat and drink to a LittleBigPlanetian and the TWEAK BUTTON is found under the Popit menu button. Just a little prod of this allows you to faff around with any object already selected.  What else? The button at the ‘bottom' … right hand side of the screen opens up the flip menus.  The top button flips your object vertically, and the left button flips it horizontally.  Then there’s the COPY BUTTON, … dashed clever this one. There it is at the bottom left of your screen. Tap that and you can make facsimiles of your object as many times as you wish.  Now before you go and create objects devices, games and levels of unfathomable ingenuity, … wit and splendour,  I want to tell you about the CONTROLLINATOR BUTTON. Whenever you get into a Controllinator you’ll notice a button in the bottom left corner of the screen.  Very handy it is as, when pressed, it ejects you from the seat allowing you renewed freedom. Brilliant, as the kids never say.  There was something else too? Oh yes, Susan wants to say hello. Go on then. <SOUND FX : Cat meow.> NARRATOR (CHUCKLE) You flirt.

434399028: Nice rocket! Very retro.  Launch that beauty into the Imagisphere and Houston would, most definitely, NOT have a problem. However, during the meticulous pre-flight test, well Sackboy jumped on it to make sure it didn’t fall over, and a problem was found! Mission control down there on the PlayStation®Vita system say it needs a new Remote Tag Sensor. What in the blue blazes is one of those?, you cry.  Well, a Remote tag Sensor let’s you detect when a tag is activated in your level either on the PlayStation®3 system or the PlayStation®Vita system. Nifty hey? To demonstrate, earlier on, Sackboy set up the Tag on the PlayStation®Vita system. What you need to do is open Popit, select the Remote Tag Sensor, and pop it on the retro rocket. The next step is to take your Popit cursor and highlight the Remote Tag Sensor.  That’s the style. Now press the TWEAK button.  Note the colours. Make sure the colour you select matches the colour of the Tag on the PlayStation®Vita system. Colour coordination is imperative for success here. Okay dokey, now wire the Remote Tag Sensor into the rocket’s Thruster. Good good. Then pick up your PlayStation®Vita system so mission control can pull that switch in 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5  --- No, I said five not fire ---but worry ye not, we have success. One small step for sack-kind, one giant leap for the LittleBigPlanet space programme which we call Sackboy’s Aerospace Share Scheme. Sounds good, but unfortunately has the acronym SASS, and that wooly hooligan is sassy enough, I thank you so very much.
